chunks: Say the Jews and the Christians: 'We are sons of God and beloved of Him.' Say: 'Why does He punish you then for your sins? No: You are only mortals, of His creation.' He can punish whom He please and pardon whom He will, for God's is the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and all that lies between them, and everything will go back to Him.
ai.seo_question: Why are Jews and Christians considered sons of God if they are punished for sins?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to refute the claim of divine sonship or exclusive favor, emphasizing that status before God is determined by piety rather than lineage. It underscores Allah's absolute sovereignty (Mulkiyyah) and free will in bestowing mercy or punishment, linking the historical Jewish and Christian claims to the broader Islamic principle that all humans are equal servants of the Creator. The verse concludes by reaffirming the ultimate return to God, reminding believers that earthly distinctions are transient compared to the eternal accountability of the Hereafter.
